test_title: PYST 19 - SSC CHSL 2025 - General Awareness (Held On: 19 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from Australia?

options.text: Advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme court
Removal of Supreme Court and High court judges

solution:
The correct answer is __**Concept of Concurrent List**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Concurrent List**: The idea of a **Concurrent List** was borrowed from the **Australian Constitution**. It allows both the Centre and the States to legislate on subjects listed under this category. 
• In the Indian Constitution, the **Concurrent List** is a part of the Seventh Schedule, which contains **52 items** (after the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976). Examples include education, marriage, adoption, and trade unions. 
• The Concurrent List ensures that both levels of government can address issues that require cooperation between the Centre and States, fostering a spirit of federalism with central oversight. Hence, this statement is correct. 
• This principle was introduced in India to ensure uniformity and consistency in legislation across various states while giving states autonomy in certain matters. 
• Australia’s Constitution also includes a Concurrent List, reflecting the federal nature of governance and ensuring shared legislative powers between the Commonwealth and States. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Amendment of the Constitution:** 
• The procedure for amendment in the Indian Constitution is inspired by the **South African Constitution**, not Australia. It involves a rigorous process requiring approval by a special majority in Parliament and, in certain cases, ratification by half of the state legislatures. Hence, this statement is incorrect. 
• Article 368 of the Indian Constitution governs the amendment process, ensuring a balance between rigidity and flexibility. 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court:** 
• This feature is derived from the **Government of India Act, 1935**, and not Australia. Article 143 of the Indian Constitution provides the President the power to seek advice from the Supreme Court on matters of public importance. Hence, this statement is incorrect. 
• The advisory jurisdiction helps resolve legal ambiguities and guides legislative and executive actions. 
• **Removal of Supreme Court and High Court Judges:** 
• The mechanism for removal of judges in India is based on the **United States Constitution**, not Australia. The process involves impeachment under Article 124(4) and Article 217(1)(b). Hence, this statement is incorrect. 
• Judges can be removed only on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity. 
• **Seventh Schedule:** 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists: **Union List, State List, and Concurrent List**. These lists define the distribution of legislative powers between the Centre and States. 
• The Concurrent List allows shared jurisdiction on subjects like education, criminal law, and marriage, ensuring cooperation between different levels of government. 
• **Federal Features of Indian Constitution:** 
• India adopted several federal principles from countries like the USA, Australia, and Canada. The Concurrent List is one such principle borrowed from Australia. 
• Other federal features include a written constitution, division of powers, and an independent judiciary. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Significance:** 
• The concept of the Concurrent List was introduced to ensure cooperative federalism and avoid conflicts between the Centre and States. 
• This list was expanded in India post the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**, demonstrating its importance in governance. 
• **Examples of Concurrent List Subjects:** 
• Education, forests, trade unions, marriage, and adoption are some subjects under the Concurrent List. 
• Legislation on these subjects requires coordination between the Centre and States to maintain uniformity. 
• **Global Influence:** 
• The Concurrent List concept has been adopted in other federal countries like Australia, emphasizing the shared legislative powers. 
• India adapted this principle to suit its unique socio-political context and governance needs.
